domain: Why two rival explanations for the decline of amateur choral singing in cities — 'busyness' versus 'atomization' — both smuggle the same unexamined idea of what singing together was ever for
topic: Why two rival explanations for the decline of amateur choral singing in cities — 'busyness' versus 'atomization' — both smuggle the same unexamined idea of what singing together was ever for

movement.gist: Open with the plain-sounding claim that community choirs are vanishing across cities, and define 'decline' as a measurable drop in participation rates — a definition that already assumes decline is the right diagnostic category.

Lay out the two standard explanations in full: the busyness thesis (modern schedules crowd out rehearsal commitments) and the atomization thesis (weakened neighborhood ties mean people no longer join anything collective, choirs included), each with supporting evidence.

Undermine both: busyness can't explain why choirs decline while equally time-demanding hobbies (running clubs, gaming leagues) grow; atomization can't explain why some intensely 'atomized' cities sustain thriving choirs. Both theories also fail to explain why the choirs that do survive don't recruit the busy or well-networked especially well.

Name the shared premise: both theories treat singing together as an instrumental good justified by the social capital it produces — a premise smuggled in by paragraph 1's very definition of 'decline' as a participation metric. Once singing is measured only as bonding-output, any explanation of its fall will look like a story about obstacles to bonding. Reframe the real question as: what happens to the act of shared, wordless coordination in a body of voices — not why participation numbers move, but why the numbers were ever the right register to watch.

poles: decline caused by time scarcity (busyness thesis)
decline caused by social fragmentation (atomization thesis)

secondary.axis: what counts as the 'real' function of communal singing
poles: singing as efficient producer of social bonds
singing as intrinsically valuable practice regardless of output

tension_system.interaction: the primary debate over causes only seems adjudicable because both sides quietly agree singing's value lies in what it produces (bonding), which is the assumption the secondary tension exposes and finally displaces

family_realization.note: Reframe_displace: busyness/atomization both fail to predict actual survivors, exposing shared bonding-output premise, pivots to coordination-as-practice.
